required_stages.description: Allocate a float32 output of M elements (or an (M, 1) buffer later viewed as (M,)) inside run().
Single read of x in which every element is converted to float32 and accumulated into float32 partial sums that are combined into one float32 total per row; masked/padded columns contribute exactly 0.
Divide each row total by the exact N in float32 (or multiply by a float32 reciprocal) and store one float32 per row; fused with the sum in the same launch.

forbidden_substitutions.message: The mean must be computed by the kernel, not by PyTorch.
Host-side row sums (sum/einsum/matmul with a ones vector) replace the reduction stage.
Host-side arithmetic on x inside run() is not part of this operator.
Casting x to float32 on the host is an untimed-equivalent extra pass; the conversion must happen inside the kernel.
A float16/bfloat16 accumulator violates the float32 accumulation requirement.
No initialised global scratch is part of this operator; partial sums must stay on chip.

required_evidence.message: No evidence of a float32 accumulator or cast inside the kernel.

outputs.aliasing: none with respect to x; the returned (M,) float32 tensor may be a metadata-only view of a buffer allocated inside run()

timing_boundary.notes: Everything inside run() is timed: the output allocation, an optional no-op contiguous() guard, the single reduction kernel and an optional metadata-only squeeze/view of the output. No cached state, no host-side cast or copy of x, no global partial-sum scratch.
